classification.difficultyReason: Calculate a trapezoidal-prism capacity, convert to litres and compare it with the available soil.

inlines.text: Jakub fills an empty flowerpot with soil. The flowerpot is a prism.
Its cross-section is a trapezium. Jakub has 2.5 litres of soil.
Does Jakub have enough soil to fill the flowerpot?

spec.description: Trapezoidal prism with depth down-right, shaded front cross-section, right face and lower connecting face; four external/internal dimension arrows.
spec.mathematics: The true trapezium has parallel sides 20 cm and 15 cm and perpendicular height 10 cm. Prism length is 20 cm. Projection is illustrative, not a scale model. Explicit faces are ABCD, EFGH, ABFE, BCGF, CDHG and DAEH; E,F,G,H are translated copies of A,B,C,D. Source-visible faces are ABCD, BCGF and CDHG. Source omits hidden edges.
spec.answerVisibility: Dimensions only; no calculated area, volume or capacity.

answer.short: No. The flowerpot holds $3.5\text{ L}$; Jakub has only $2.5\text{ L}$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{10}{2}(15+20)\\A&=175\text{ cm}^2\\V&=Ah\\V&=175\times20\\V&=3500\text{ cm}^3\\\text{Capacity}&=3500\text{ mL}\\\text{Capacity}&=3.5\text{ L}\end{align*}$$
Jakub has $2.5\text{ L}<3.5\text{ L}$, so he does not have enough soil.
